summary: Treat bare write operands as paths
body: When a lane runs `cd ~/other-project && touch newfile` or `mkdir newdir`, the new basename is neither an existing path nor slash- or extension-shaped, so this predicate drops it and records no write. Because the path is outside the target repository, the main-checkout scan cannot catch it, and the point can be logged clean. Treat non-option operands of known write commands as paths, or fail closed; this violates [D8](https://github.com/brindlewick/postmaster/blob/665a99f9d9c08e69c101d7fbfa927afc79b4f231/WORKHORSE-SPEC.md#L36).

summary: Mark unparsed MCP calls as unchecked
body: If a Codex lane uses a filesystem-capable MCP tool whose path is nested under `arguments`, this branch counts the call, but `directCallTouches` only looks for top-level path fields and a command. `readLane` therefore marks the stream checked without recording the write; writes outside the target repository can then pass unnoticed. Parse nested arguments or mark MCP calls without a usable path reader as not checked, consistent with [D8 and D13](https://github.com/brindlewick/postmaster/blob/665a99f9d9c08e69c101d7fbfa927afc79b4f231/WORKHORSE-SPEC.md#L36-L41).

summary: Redact paths from not-checked card reasons
body: If a supported lane's shell input contains an unresolvable absolute glob, the reader includes that raw token in the `not checked` reason. This branch prints the reason verbatim instead of applying `reachPath`, so the ship card can expose a home or other-project path in a public pull request. Redact paths in the diagnostic while keeping the full value in the run log, as required by [D18](https://github.com/brindlewick/postmaster/blob/665a99f9d9c08e69c101d7fbfa927afc79b4f231/WORKHORSE-SPEC.md#L46).
